title: H3 Base Ref2VA capability, style and FaceSwap controls

tests.assessment: Valid neutral control: photoreal woman, clear left-to-right head turn, stable medium close-up and studio background.
tests.prompt: A woman in a plain dark jacket stands in a quiet studio and slowly turns her head from left to right, then looks directly at the camera. Medium close-up, steady camera, even daylight, simple gray background.

tests.assessment: Picture reached Ref2VA, but stained glass, leaded edges and glass material did not transfer. Output stayed photoreal; only incidental subject/background details changed.
tests.prompt: A woman in a plain dark jacket stands in a quiet studio and slowly turns her head from left to right, then looks directly at the camera. Medium close-up, steady camera, even daylight, simple gray background.
tests.contextInstruction: Use <Picture 1> as the visual/style reference for rendering.

tests.assessment: Strong transfer of the reference woman's short black hair, facial structure and makeup. This verifies identity/appearance conditioning, not a distinct style mechanism.
tests.prompt: A woman in a plain dark jacket stands in a quiet studio and slowly turns her head from left to right, then looks directly at the camera. Medium close-up, steady camera, even daylight, simple gray background.
tests.contextInstruction: Use <Picture 1> as the visual/style reference for rendering.
observationPrompts: Difference from S1 at fixed seed

tests.variable: two Pictures with separated subject/style roles
tests.assessment: Picture 1 identity dominates. Picture 2 stained-glass rendering is not visible, so subject/style role separation is limited and style remains unverified.
tests.prompt: A woman in a plain dark jacket stands in a quiet studio and slowly turns her head from left to right, then looks directly at the camera. Medium close-up, steady camera, even daylight, simple gray background.
tests.contextInstruction: Use <Picture 1> for subject identity and appearance. Use <Picture 2> only for artistic style and rendering.

tests.variable: three Pictures / order and multi-image conditioning
tests.assessment: All three image tensors reached conditioning in numbered order. Output remains dominated by Picture 1 identity; weak palette shifts are not proof that each requested semantic role was separated.
tests.prompt: A woman in a plain dark jacket stands in a quiet studio and slowly turns her head from left to right, then looks directly at the camera. Medium close-up, steady camera, even daylight, simple gray background.
tests.contextInstruction: Use <Picture 1> for subject identity. Use <Picture 2> for stained-glass rendering. Use <Picture 3> only for the restrained warm-gray palette and background treatment.

tests.assessment: Head-turn timing, framing, pose progression and static camera closely track A0. Video motion conditioning is verified.
tests.prompt: A woman in a plain dark jacket stands in a quiet studio and slowly turns her head from left to right, then looks directly at the camera. Medium close-up, steady camera, even daylight, simple gray background.
tests.contextInstruction: Use <Video 1> only for motion, timing, framing and camera movement.
observationPrompts: Appearance leakage from grayscale motion guide

tests.assessment: Video motion/framing is preserved. Picture influence is weak compared with video identity, so mixed Picture+Video works technically but role balance is limited.
tests.prompt: A woman in a plain dark jacket stands in a quiet studio and slowly turns her head from left to right, then looks directly at the camera. Medium close-up, steady camera, even daylight, simple gray background.
tests.contextInstruction: Use <Picture 1> for subject appearance. Use <Video 1> for motion, timing and camera movement.

tests.assessment: Plain Ref2VA control preserves source identity and performance despite the identity Picture being present.
tests.prompt: Preserve the source performance, pose, timing, framing and camera. The person slowly turns toward the camera in a plain studio.
tests.contextInstruction: Use <Video 1> for the performance. Use <Picture 1> as the facial identity reference.

tests.variable: FaceSwap modifier ON at upstream strength 1
tests.assessment: FaceSwap visibly replaces identity as the face turns toward camera while preserving motion/framing. Frontal result is strong; profile and transition frames are temporally inconsistent, so capability is verified but limited.
tests.prompt: Preserve the source performance, pose, timing, framing and camera. The person slowly turns toward the camera in a plain studio.
tests.contextInstruction: Use <Video 1> for the performance. Use <Picture 1> as the facial identity reference.

tests.variable: FaceSwap OFF immediately after ON / contamination control
tests.assessment: Byte-identical to F0 (same SHA-256 and SSIM 1.0) without worker restart. No dynamic LoRA contamination.
tests.prompt: Preserve the source performance, pose, timing, framing and camera. The person slowly turns toward the camera in a plain studio.
tests.contextInstruction: Use <Video 1> for the performance. Use <Picture 1> as the facial identity reference.
observationPrompts: Worker stayed up between F1 and F2
